item.title: Surrogate mom discovers baby’s dad is Chinese billionaire with 300 US-born kids seeking a Musk match
item.description: A Chinese billionaire is allegedly engaging in American surrogacy to have more than a hundred children, raising significant ethical concerns. One surrogate discovered that her intended father had multiple surrogacy arrangements already in progress. This scenario underscores a troubling lack of transparency in the surrogacy sector, prompting vital discussions on surrogate rights and the necessity for clearer disclosure from intended parents.

item.title: In 1985, Rick Hansen began a 40,075-km journey; 40 years later, his barrier-free vision lives on
item.description: Rick Hansen embarked on an extraordinary journey in 1985, covering more than 40,000 kilometers to raise vital awareness and funds for individuals with disabilities. This monumental tour sparked a global movement advocating for accessibility, which continues through the Rick Hansen Foundation today. Their focus now includes programs on accessibility certification and fostering youth leadership, all aimed at building truly inclusive communities that everyone can enjoy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Couple finds aquifer near ocean, now the water sells for $10
item.description: In South Australia, a couple stumbled upon a remarkable underground aquifer beneath their land, launching them into the world of fine-water production. Garnering a flawless 100 points from global judges, their bottled water highlights a rising trend in consumer preference for pure, mineral-rich beverages. This phenomenon redefines traditional perceptions of water, transforming it from a mere commodity into a sought-after luxury.

item.title: US may swap federal land on Georgia’s Cumberland Island for private parcels; conservation rules could reshape what happens next
item.description: The National Park Service is evaluating the possibility of land exchanges on Cumberland Island. The strategy involves acquiring privately owned parcels in exchange for federal lands, which will continue to be protected under conservation restrictions. The agency invites public input regarding the possible environmental repercussions of this initiative, which aims to enhance the management and consolidation of safeguarded areas on the island.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Homeless man’s viral church piano performance raises $50,000 for charity, helps him find a home
item.description: In January 2024, homeless man Rhys Wynne-Jones went to a church in England for shelter and asked to play its piano. His performance of Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody” went viral. Two years later, he has found a home, performed at charity events, worked with Peter Andre and raised more than £40,000 for homeless charities and other good causes.

item.title: In 1869, 100 sheep became 5,000 on Socorro Island; 1,762 removed as forest-habitat vegetation cover rose 29%-85%
item.description: Feral sheep introduced to Socorro Island caused severe ecological damage over decades. An eradication program removed 1,762 sheep between 2009 and 2012. Vegetation cover and soil conditions began recovering surprisingly quickly after grazing pressure ceased. This recovery demonstrated the island's remarkable ecological resilience and capacity for self-repair. However, other invasive species like feral cats remain a significant conservation challenge.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists taught bald ibises migration by microlight; Europe saw its first colony in 400 years
item.description: Conservationists successfully reintroduced northern bald ibises to Europe after centuries of absence. Young birds were trained to follow microlight aircraft south to Italy for winter. This innovative method helped them relearn ancient migration routes and return independently. By 2011, the birds began returning without human guidance, establishing a self-sustaining colony. Further management interventions are still needed to ensure the species' long-term viability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How Singapore turned garbage ash into a 350-hectare island where mangroves and coral now flourish
item.description: Singapore has pioneered a remarkable 350-hectare landfill created from incinerated waste, known as Semakau Landfill. This innovative site not only manages the nation’s scarce land but also provides a habitat for diverse marine life. With migratory birds nesting and corals thriving, this man-made island exemplifies successful waste management, projected to remain operational until 2035.

item.title: He paid 75 cents for a record, and sold it for $25,200 later
item.description: A collector discovered a rare Velvet Underground acetate in 2002. This recording contained early versions of songs from their debut album. He later sold the acetate for $25,200 to an anonymous buyer. The acetate's existence remained largely unknown for many years. A remastered version was eventually released to the public.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1966, a thrift-store painting cost under $100; 60 years later, it sold for £189,200
item.description: In 1966, retired art teacher Helene Plotkin bought a painting for less than $100 at a thrift store in New York. Nearly 60 years later, the work was identified as an FCB Cadell painting. After her son researched it and AI helped decipher the signature, the artwork sold for £189,200 at auction in Edinburgh.
